$comment: Five regions, and the tone each one is drawn in when there is no photograph. The tone is a design decision recorded as data rather than typed into a stylesheet, and it is the reason a country without a picture still looks like somewhere: every unresolved slot is drawn on its own region's ground, so moving from the Sahel to the Cape changes the colour of the page even before a photograph exists. All five sit inside the Afrinkong palette — they are values of the same ink, not five new brand colours — and none of them claims anything about the place beyond what its own terrain words already say.

central.name: Central & West
central.line: Rainforest, volcanic coast, savanna, ancient kingdoms and the cultures of the Gulf of Guinea.
central.tone_note: Rainforest and volcanic ground: the darkest, greenest tone in the set.

east.name: East Africa
east.line: The Rift, the great migrations, the gorilla forests, Kilimanjaro, the Nile and the Swahili coast.
east.tone_note: The Rift and the montane forest — green, but lifted and cooler than the Congo basin.

southern.name: Southern Africa
southern.line: The Namib, the Zambezi, the Kalahari, the Cape, and wilderness you walk rather than drive.
southern.tone_note: Desert, delta and Kalahari sand: the warm ochre end.

north.name: North Africa
north.line: The Atlas, the Sahara, the Nile, and Mediterranean cities older than most countries.
north.tone_note: Atlas stone, Sahara and mud-brick — pale clay.

islands.name: Islands
islands.line: Indian Ocean reef, granite and volcanic islands, and an ecology that evolved on its own.
islands.tone_note: Reef and lagoon: the one tone in the set that leans blue.
